title: Asha and the Rhyming Blight
markdown:
The sun painted stripes across Asha’s bedroom floor, each one a brilliant burst of gold. Birdsong tapped a bouncy beat against her window. Today felt special. It buzzed with an exciting ticklish energy, like a thousand tiny butterflies doing somersaults in her tummy.

She hopped out of bed, feet tapping a quick happy rhythm.

“Good morning, Sprig.”

From under her bed a fluffy blur of brown and white shot out like a tiny rocket. Sprig the broom rabbit. Whiskers twitching with pure delight, long ears flapping. He nudged her ankle, a clear silent signal that breakfast was ready and, most importantly, the broom needed its essential morning fluffing. Sprig took his fluffing duties very seriously.

But as Asha reached for her trusty spellcasting book and her favorite shimmering quill, something was odd. Very odd. Her math problems. Instead of neat rows of numbers, they were wiggly giggly words.

“Two plus two equals… what a pretty view.” Her brow furrowed just a tiny bit.

“This cannot be right.” Sprig squeaked, ears flopping dramatically. He nudged the book as if trying to nudge the numbers back into place.

“Seven times eight equals… such a happy date.” Asha giggled, then her smile faded. “This is Sprig’s tidying, isn’t it? He was helping me organize my desk last night, but this is way too much tidying.”

A tiny shimmering ink blot, no bigger than her thumb and pulsing with a faint mischievous glow, quivered near the edge of the page. Practically giggling. Then, with a quick dart, it zipped across the page, leaving a glittering trail of rhyming magic. History transformed: the Battle of Big Boots involved very large silly suits. Potion-making notes became a ridiculous chant. For bubbly brew, add a happy leaping kangaroo.

The ink blot, with a flourish, zoomed out of the book and zipped across the room, a tiny black streak of silliness.

“It’s a Rhyming Blight.” Asha’s eyes sparkled with determined mischief. “And we absolutely have to catch it before it turns all my schoolwork into nonsense.”

Sprig bounced, fluffy tail twitching. “Catch it? How? It’s so speedy. A little black blur.”

“With speed, Sprig. And a bit of sparkle.” She grabbed her broom, which gave a happy excited whizz as she swung onto it. Sprig, with a practiced hop, landed right behind her, clinging tight, whiskers tickling her ear. “Hold on tight.” A mighty kick, and they burst into the hallway.

Down the hallway they zoomed, the blot a little black dot zipping ahead, a trail of shimmering words in its wake. It bounced off the walls with a soft thwip, leaving tiny rhyming splatters that seemed to whisper: your socks are so neat, right down to your feet.

“We’ve got to pin it down.” Asha maneuvered around a tall vase. The blot dived into the kitchen, where the toasty smell of fresh bread tickled their noses. It splattered the shiny toaster. Toast is so warm, safe from any storm.

“Silly rhyming ink blot.” Sprig giggled, a tinkling bell. He loved a good rhyme, but this was too much chaos.

They chased it into the garden, dewdrops sparkling like a billion tiny diamonds. The sweet clean scent of morning blossoms. The blot did a loop-de-loop around a bright red tulip. Tulips so bright, a truly dazzling sight.

“Almost got it.” Asha tilted the broom, swooping low. Sprig leaped from her shoulders, landing with a soft thump right in front of the blot, blocking its path.

“Not so fast, you little rhyming rascal.” His fluffy tail puffed like a proud pom-pom.

The blot tried one last desperate rhyme. A rabbit so fluffy, making things quite stuffy.

But Asha was already there. She gently scooped the tiny giggling blot into a special empty potion bottle she kept handy. It jiggled inside, trying to rhyme its way out. This bottle so clear, oh dear, oh dear, I’m stuck in here.

“Gotcha.” She capped it with a satisfying twist. The rhyming stopped instantly. The blot looked a little sad, glow dimming. It had not meant to cause trouble. It just loved to play with words.

“We did it.” Sprig bounced on the broom, whiskers quivering with pride. He gave Asha’s shoulder a happy nudge.

She patted his head. “Brilliant work, Sprig. Now, back to those lessons.” She winked, holding up the bottle. “This time they’ll make perfect sensible sense.”

They zipped back into the house, sunbeams dancing. Homework was numbers and facts again. History was dates and battles, not big boots and silly suits. Asha did not declare the day amazing. She only set the bottle on the windowsill where the blot could still see the garden, and opened her book to a page that, for now, refused to rhyme.
